reasoning_trace.description: MANDATORY: You MUST describe what you see in the images (Charts, System Models) to prove you have analyzed them.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper proposes a DCO-OFDM scheme for FSO-ISAC, which combines communication and sensing functionalities within an individual system. The system model is based on a LiDAR, which provides active sensing abilities for both cooperative and uncooperative targets. The DCO-OFDM signal model is introduced, and the clipping noise is modeled as additive colored Gaussian noise (ACGN) to elicit an equivalent frequency-selective channel for FSO-ISAC.

reasoning_trace.description: Explain the System Mechanism and ISAC Coupling Mode found.
reasoning_trace.value: The system mechanism is based on the DCO-OFDM scheme, which adds a direct-current (DC) bias to the original OFDM signal to obtain a nonnegative signal. The ISAC coupling mode is achieved through the joint optimization of communication and sensing performance metrics, which are derived based on the equivalent frequency-selective channel model.

reasoning_trace.description: Validate the physical consistency of reported metrics (Rate/Resolution).
reasoning_trace.value: The paper provides numerical simulations to evaluate the proposed DCO-OFDM scheme for FSO-ISAC. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms and reveal the tradeoff between communication and sensing functionalities. The sensing precision is shown to be robust to channel variations, and the computational complexity of the proposed algorithms is analyzed.

reasoning_trace.description: Identify the solved problems and remaining open challenges.
reasoning_trace.value: The paper solves the problem of joint optimization of communication and sensing performance metrics for FSO-ISAC. However, open challenges remain, such as the extension of the proposed scheme to multitarget scenarios and the investigation of novel performance metrics for various sensing tasks. Additionally, the development of robust and cost-effective beamforming schemes for optical sensors is an open challenge.
